chunks: He accompanied a funeral and heard a man laughing.

Then he said: It is as if death has been ordained only for others, and it is as if the right is obligatory only on others, and it is as if those whom we see among the dead have departed on a journey and will return to us shortly.
We place them in their graves and consume their inheritance, as if we will live forever after them.
Then we have forgotten every preacher, man or woman, and have been struck by every major catastrophe.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about human arrogance when seeing a funeral?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the juxtaposition of a funeral and a laughing bystander to critique the human tendency toward *ghurur* (self-delusion) and the belief in immortality. He highlights how people view death as a distant event for others while assuming they will inherit the deceased's wealth, leading to spiritual negligence until struck by sudden calamities. This reflection underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *mawt* (death) as a constant companion to the believer, serving as a corrective to the arrogance of the living.
